setup.title: Get the extension running.
setup.intro:
Follow the steps below to import the Streamer.bot actions, enable them, add the overlay to OBS, and configure the extension.

 Click [[code:Copy Import Code]] to copy the complete RTS import code, or [[overlay:Copy Overlay URL]] to copy the hosted browser-source URL.

steps.title: Import the extension into Streamer.bot
steps.description:
Start by importing the supplied RTS actions into Streamer.bot.

 The quickest method is to click [[code:Copy Import Code]] to copy the complete import code, then paste it into Streamer.bot's Import dialog.

substeps.title: Copy the import code
substeps.text:
Click [[code:Copy Import Code]] to copy the complete RTS import code to your clipboard.

 You will paste this code into the Streamer.bot Import dialog.

images.alt: The RTS extension import code with an arrow pointing to the import code button

substeps.title: Open Import
substeps.text:
In Streamer.bot, click **Import** from the toolbar.

 This opens the Import dialog where you can paste the RTS import code you copied in the previous step.

 [[muted:If you are using Streamer.bot version 1.0.0 or later, you can also select **File > Import** from the menu bar.]]

  After pasting in the code Click the Import Button.

[[muted:If you are using Streamer.bot version 1.0.7 or later, you will be taken to the next step automatically without the need to click the Import button.]]

images.alt: Streamer.bot import screen showing the RTS extension import code

substeps.title: Review The imported actions and commands
substeps.text:
After the import code is pasted, Streamer.bot will show a confirmation dialog with the actions and commands that will be imported.

 Review the actions and commands to ensure they are correct.

 If everything looks correct, click **Import** to complete the import.

substeps.title: Confirm the import once more!
substeps.text:
Streamer.bot will show you a warning that the imported actions contain Custom C# code.

 This is the code that powers RTS Extensions.

 Click **Import** to confirm again!

steps.title: Enable the imported actions
steps.description: Enable the imported RTS actions so the extension can respond to ban and timeout events.

substeps.title: Enable the extension actions
substeps.text:
In Streamer.bot, enable the imported RTS actions.

 The actions need to be enabled before the extension can respond to events.

images.alt: Streamer.bot imported RTS actions being enabled

substeps.title: Check and enable the commands
substeps.text:
Open the **Commands** section and confirm the imported RTS commands are present.

 Enable any commands that you want the extension to use.

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS extension commands

substeps.title: Set up the Streamer.bot WebSocket Server
substeps.text:
Streamer.bots built in websocket server is what passes events to the overlay, you will need to turn it on so the overlay can respond to events.

 In the left panel select Servers / Clients [[muted:Right down at the bottom of the list]].

 Select WebSocket Server, Turn Auto Start on [[muted:So you don't have to turn it on each time Streamer.bot starts]]. 

 Set the Port to 8080 [[muted:This is the default port for the extension, but you can change it if needed]]. 

 Click Start Server, [[muted:If you have Auto Start on then this will start automatically each time Streamer.bot starts]]

steps.title: Add the extension overlay to OBS
steps.description:
Add the hosted RTS overlay as an OBS Browser Source.

 The hosted overlay is the recommended option because it keeps the overlay files up to date automatically.

substeps.title: Copy the overlay URL
substeps.text:
Click [[overlay:Copy Overlay URL]] to copy the hosted browser-source URL to your clipboard.

 You will paste this URL into the OBS Browser Source settings.

images.alt: RTS copy overlay URL button screenshot

substeps.title: Create a browser source
substeps.text:
In OBS, add a **Browser** source to an existing scene or create a new scene for the extension overlay.

 Depending on your version of OBS, The interface for doing this may differ from the image.

 You can either: 

 right-click in the **Sources** panel and select **Add > Browser** 

 Or 

 Click the **+** button in the **Sources** panel and select **Browser**.

images.alt: OBS add a new browser source dialog

substeps.title: Configure the browser source
substeps.text:
Paste the URL you copied into the **URL** field.

 Set the [[muted:width]] and [[muted:height]] to [[yellow:**1920 × 1080**]], or use your screen resolution if different. [[yellow:Make sure you use a 16:9 aspect ratio]] so the overlay is not distorted.

 If you wish to control the volume of the audio via OBS, then check the [[muted:Control audio via OBS]] option.

steps.title: Configure settings and test the extension
steps.description: Open the RTS extension settings and run the built-in test trigger before using the extension live.

substeps.title: Open the settings dialog
substeps.text:
In the **Actions** panel, find the **Extensions Settings Action**.

Select the trigger called **Core Test**, right-click it, then choose **Test Trigger** to open the extension settings dialog.

 If you have never used an RTS Extension before and have not yet installed the [[dll:RtsUI.dll]] or are using an older version of the [[muted:DLL]]

 You will be prompted to have it to Installed or Updated. 

 Once the settings dialog has loaded then [[muted:Save and Exit]] to close initiate the settings used by the extension.

substeps.title: Do a Timeout test
substeps.text:
In the **Actions** panel, find the **RTS- Ban / Timeout - Timeout Action**.

Select the trigger called **Twitch Moderation**,

 Right-click it, then choose **Simulate** to simulate a Twitch Timeout.

 Look at the overlay to see the user locked up in a cage!!!

 [[muted:If you do not see anything then make sure you have set up the Streamer.bot WebSocket Server correctly and it is running]]

images.alt: Test a simulated Twitch timeout trigger

substeps.title: Do a Ban test
substeps.text:
In the **Actions** panel, find the **RTS- Ban / Timeout - Ban Action**.

Select the trigger called **Twitch Moderation**,

 Right-click it, then choose **Simulate** to simulate a Twitch Timeout.

 Look at the overlay to see the get driven off to the gulag!!!

 [[muted:If you do not see anything then make sure you have set up the Streamer.bot WebSocket Server correctly and it is running]]

images.alt: Test a simulated Twitch ban trigger

substeps.title: Automatic installation of RTS UI DLL
substeps.text:
[[yellow:If the RTS UI DLL is not installed]], the extension can download it and place it in your Streamer.bot installation directory.

For more information, see the [[DLL:RTS UI DLL installation page]].

substeps.title: Automatic updating of RTS UI DLL
substeps.text:
If the extension requires a newer version of the RTS UI DLL, it will ask whether you want to download and install the latest version.

[[muted:The extension will only request an update when the installed version is below the required version.]]
